q.intro.text: A jacket is twenty percent off. The sale price is forty-eight dollars.

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the notation.

e.s1.text: The original price is the whole: one hundred percent. Twenty percent came off, so forty-eight dollars is eighty percent of it, four of its five equal sections.

e.s2.text: Forty-eight dollars is four sections. One section is forty-eight divided by four: twelve dollars.

e.s3.text: The original is all five sections: five times twelve dollars is sixty dollars.

e.s4.text: In one step: the sale price is zero point eight times the original, so the original is forty-eight dollars divided by zero point eight: sixty dollars.

e.why.text: Quick check: why divide by zero point eight, and not add twenty percent of forty-eight dollars back?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. The twenty percent was twenty percent of the original. Forty-eight dollars is only eighty percent of it, so dividing by zero point eight gets back to one hundred percent.

e.w-back.text: Twenty percent of forty-eight dollars is only nine dollars and sixty cents, which gives fifty-seven sixty. The twenty percent came off the bigger original: twenty percent of sixty dollars is twelve dollars.

e.w-rate.text: Forty-eight divided by zero point two is two hundred forty dollars, five times too much. Forty-eight dollars is eighty percent of the original, so divide by zero point eight.

t.intro.text: Now a concert ticket costs fifty-four dollars in total, with eight percent sales tax. The first step is done for you.

t.whole.text: The price before tax is the whole, one hundred percent. The tax adds eight percent, so the total is one hundred eight percent of the price.

t.mult.text: Your step: the total is what number times the price before tax?

t.m-ok.text: Yes: one hundred eight percent is one point zero eight. The total is one point zero eight times the price.

t.m-rate.text: Zero point zero eight is only the tax. The total is the price plus the tax: one plus zero point zero eight.

t.m-dir.text: Tax makes the total bigger than the price, so the multiplier is more than one.

t.m-pct.text: One hundred eight percent is right, but write it as a decimal: one hundred eight hundredths.

t.m-other.text: The total is one hundred eight percent of the price. Write one hundred eight percent as a decimal.

t.div.text: Your step: divide. What was the price before tax?

t.d-ok.text: Yes: fifty-four dollars divided by one point zero eight is fifty dollars.

t.d-opp.text: That takes eight percent of fifty-four dollars off: the wrong base. The eight percent was of the price before tax. Divide by one point zero eight.

t.d-rate.text: That divides by the tax rate. Fifty-four dollars is one hundred eight percent of the price, so divide by one point zero eight.

t.d-fwd.text: That adds the tax a second time. To undo it, divide by one point zero eight.

t.d-num.text: Eight percent is not eight dollars. Divide fifty-four dollars by one point zero eight.

t.d-other.text: Fifty-four dollars is one point zero eight times the price. Divide fifty-four dollars by one point zero eight.

t.check.text: Now check it. Which one is a real check?

t.c-ok.text: Yes: eight percent of fifty dollars is four dollars, and fifty plus four is fifty-four. Going forward lands on the total.

t.c-repeat.text: Doing the same division again repeats any slip. Check by going forward from your answer.

t.c-opp.text: Eight percent of fifty-four dollars uses the total as the base. It gives forty-nine sixty-eight, not fifty, even though fifty dollars is right.

t.c-less.text: Being less than fifty-four dollars only checks the direction. Many wrong prices pass that.

t.cb-right.text: At the start you picked sixty dollars, and you were right. Now you can show why.

t.cb-576.text: At the start you picked fifty-seven sixty: that adds twenty percent of forty-eight dollars, the wrong base. The original was sixty dollars.

t.cb-68.text: At the start you picked sixty-eight dollars: that adds twenty dollars, not twenty percent. The original was sixty dollars.

t.cb-none.text: At the start: forty-eight dollars is eighty percent of the original, so the original was forty-eight divided by zero point eight, sixty dollars.

p.intro.text: A store marks a sixty dollar skateboard up twenty-five percent to seventy-five dollars. Theo says: take twenty-five percent off seventy-five dollars and you are back at sixty. Is Theo right?

p.test.text: Let's test it. Build the argument and see where it leads.

p.prove.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.c1.text: The markup was twenty-five percent of sixty dollars, that is fifteen dollars, because a percent change is a percent of the amount before the change.

p.c2.text: but twenty-five percent off seventy-five dollars is twenty-five percent of seventy-five, that is eighteen seventy-five, because after the markup the base is seventy-five dollars, and the same percent of a bigger base is more.

p.c3.text: so it leaves fifty-six twenty-five, not sixty. The way back is seventy-five divided by one point two five, sixty dollars, because seventy-five dollars is one hundred twenty-five percent of the original.

p.x-cancel.text: Up twenty-five percent and down twenty-five percent would only cancel if both were percents of the same amount. They are not.

p.x-near.text: Fifty-six twenty-five is not a rounding gap: every amount here is exact. Three seventy-five is missing.

p.x-rate.text: Dividing by zero point two five gives three hundred dollars. Seventy-five dollars is one hundred twenty-five percent of the original, so divide by one point two five.

p.x-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line.

p.done.text: That's a proof: each claim has its reason, and the tapes back every one. Theo used the new price as the base.
